stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Bartolome de las Casas, A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies (written 1542, published 1552). Las Casas wrote that the peoples of Hispaniola were gentle and obedient, owning little, and that the Spanish fell upon them like wolves, killing them and forcing them into hard labor. He claimed the Indigenous population of Hispaniola had fallen from about three million to only two hundred, and he sent the account to Prince Philip of Spain to persuade the crown to stop the cruelty.

parts.prompt: Identify Las Casas's purpose in writing this account.
Explain how Las Casas's description of Indigenous peoples supports his argument.
Explain one reason a historian might question the population figures Las Casas gives.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
